newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's PIA to upgrade, expand fleet.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's PIA to upgrade, expand fleet.

text.p: Pakistan International Airline Corporation (PIA) plans to expand its fleet and replace some of its aircraft to cope with growing passenger traffic, a company official said on Monday.
"PIA is working on the plan to identify the measures necessary for carrying out the replacement of its ageing aircraft, especially the B747-200 fleet," managing director Nawaz Tiwana told Reuters.
PIA was considering the Boeing 747-400, Boeing 777, MD-11, Airbus A340 and used B747-300s as possible replacements and proposals could go to PIA's board in the next two months.
The airline now has eight Boeing 747-200s, nine Airbus A300-B4s, six Airbus A310-300s, six Boeing 737-300s, two Boeing 707 cargo planes, 13 Fokker F-27s and two Twin Otters.

Tiwana said the 747s should be replaced before older planes such as the F-27s "because 747s are really the money-makers for this company". He put the cost of replacing the entire 747 fleet with new 747-400s at about $1.5 billion. Second-hand aircraft would cost slightly more than half that amount.
Tiwana said PIA had recently brought an Airbus A300-B4 aircraft into its fleet on dry lease with an option to buy.

It planned to acquire two B737-300s and two Airbus A300-B4s within five years to cope with growth in short-to-medium range routes. Replacement aircraft for the B747-200s would also meet expected growth on long-range international routes.
"In case PIA purchases brand-new aircraft from manufacturers, we would expect full support from the relevant export credit agencies for the financing of such acquisitions," Tiwana said.
"In case PIA purchases used aircraft, we would expect to raise the necessary funds from international capital markets."
He said PIA's domestic passenger traffic grew seven percent from July to December of last year, against a previous annual average of three percent. This meant more capacity might be needed.

Tiwana said the airline was hoping to expand revenue by seven percent to help it recover from past financial losses, partly due to competition with local airlines that had grabbed 30 to 40 percent of domestic business.
PIA's after-tax profit plunged to 65 million rupees in 1995/96 (July-June) from 293 million in the year-earlier period.
PIA paid no dividend or bonus stocks for the year ended June 30. Its 10-rupee share closed 0.45 rupee up at 9.50 on Sunday.
Tiwana said new routes were planned to South Korea, Australia, South Africa, Spain and China, but gave no details.
He said PIA felt that its profitability and operational strength should be upgraded before any privatisation plan is implemented.
